points.why: It does not name the Attractiveness Principle, but it describes a series of shared limits (review, CI, chat, release, governance) binding one after another as the project grows.
It says outright that relieving one constraint just moves the bottleneck to the next shared resource.
It frames the decision as choosing how much volume to want and deliberately accepting gatekeeping and fragmentation, but never says that not choosing lets whichever limit binds first decide.

pitfalls.why: It explicitly links the bottlenecks to one shared, coupled structure rather than treating them as unrelated.

notes: The claim that coordination cost grows with possible interactions is asserted loosely but is not harmful.
